name: David
overview: David was a male from the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Jesse and the King of Israel. His life and reign are foundational in the biblical history of Israel, marking him as a central figure in God's redemptive plan. The biblical record highlights his role as a leader and servant of the LORD.
namesAndTitles: The name David means 'beloved one,' reflecting his favored status. He is also known by several titles such as 'My servant David,' 'His Anointed,' and 'My King,' which are given by God and emphasize his divine appointment and relationship with the LORD. Other titles like 'King of Judah' and 'King of Israel' denote his royal authority and leadership over God's people.
familyAndRelationships: David is recorded as the son of Jesse and husband to Michal, Abigail, Ahinoam, Maacah, Haggith, Abital, and Eglah. He is the father of Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, and Ithream. Importantly, he is explicitly described as a servant of YHVH, underscoring his spiritual role and submission to God.
scriptureSignificance: David's significance lies in his establishment as the king chosen by God to lead Israel, uniting the nation and founding Jerusalem as the political and spiritual center. Despite personal failings, he is recognized as a man after God's own heart and is the ancestor from whom the promised Messiah would come. His life and reign set the stage for the fulfillment of God's covenant and the coming of Christ, the 'Son of David.'
